text:
maya: Quick async sync — onboarding `aurora-rt-13b-v2` weights to prod S3 + a tokenizer quirk popped up, and I want to lock the continuous-batching + cache defaults before the canary.
jonathan: ack. which S3 path? do we have checksums?
maya: s3://redwood-models/aurora/13b/v2/weights/* — latest manifest is `v2-manifest.json` (sha256 listed). I pasted the manifest in the deploy PR.
kevin: saw a small tokenizer mismatch in local tests — model's tokenizer maps `<pad>` -> token id 0 but EOF handling expects `` token id 2 in our runtime. falling back to library default causes off-by-one in alignments.
sarah: oof. is that just a special token name difference or actual id skew?
kevin: name difference only but downstream code checks for `eos_id == 2`. quick fix: runtime should look up tokens by name with fallback, not assume ids. patch in review: `runtime/tokenizer/fallback_eos_fix`.
maya: thanks. can we patch before the canary? I'd rather not roll with a manual token id map.
jonathan: +1 for runtime fix. can we also add a validation job in the onboarding pipeline that runs a small decode sanity test (prompt -> expected suffix) and checksum token ids?
kei (deploy-bot): :information_source: canary deployment scheduled at 2026-07-12T03:00:00Z if all checks pass.
rui: for the batching/caching defaults: we previously used `continuous_batching.window_ms=12` and `scheduler.prefetch=2`. For this model, latency/throughput sweet spot looks like window_ms=8 and prefetch=4 in perf runs. but cache.policy needs tightening — prefix-KV caching with TTL 30s caused stale prefix hits on conversation resets.
sarah: sounds reasonable. what's the implication for max_tokens? earlier models needed `max_tokens_per_request=2048` but aurora has 8192 context, we should cap per-request to 4096 by default to avoid huge KV memory blowouts.
kevin: agree on 4096 default. also recommend `batch.max_tokens_total=65536` so the scheduler can pack but not overcommit.
maya: can someone propose the minimal config diff we can ship with the canary? I want to include it in the PR description.
jonathan: here's a draft snippet to validate in CI: ```json
{
  "continuous_batching": { "window_ms": 8, "max_batch_size": 16 },
  "scheduler": { "prefetch": 4, "max_inflight": 64 },
  "cache": { "policy": "prefix_kv", "prefix_ttl_s": 30, "validate_on_hit": true },
  "limits": { "max_tokens_per_request": 4096, "batch_max_tokens_total": 65536 }
}
```
maya: looks good. add `validate_on_hit=true` helps detect stale prefixes. can we also add a CI check that runs token-id mapping validation? sample command: `./ci/check_token_map.sh aurora-rt-13b-v2 s3://redwood-models/aurora/13b/v2/weights/`
kevin: that script is ready, but it currently exits nonzero on mismatch which will block canary. fine by me. it's in the PR under `.ci/token_map_check`.
jonathan: I'll add a small integration test to `onboard-validation` that runs a 16-token prompt and asserts the final token sequence contains the expected eos name.
sarah: who will own the canary monitoring? I can set up a dashboard with token-level latency and cache hit ratio and a small regression alert if generation divergence > 1.5% vs baseline.
maya: assign to sarah for dashboards, jonathan for CI test, kevin for runtime tokenizer patch, and me to coordinate canary PR + manifest pin.
rui: pinging @eng-sre for capacity review — `max_inflight=64` might be high for the initial canary. maybe reduce to 24 for first 24h.
jonathan: good call. we'll set canary overrides: `max_inflight=24` and ramp to 64 after 6h if ops OK. document in PR.
maya: perfect. final checklist: weights manifest present, token_map_check green, runtime patch merged, config JSON in PR, canary override included, dashboards wired. Anyone blocking?
kevin: no blockers from runtime side, will land patch in the next hour.
sarah: will have dashboards up before canary.
rui: SRE will review capacity, should be fine.
maya: thanks all — I'll update the PR and tag the canary schedule. :thumbsup:
jonathan: ping me for code review when PR ready, will do a quick look asap.
deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: preflight checks passed: manifest present, digest verified, config schema valid.
